verdict.rationale: LiteLLM is a self-hosted proxy, so the operator decides where it and its data live. Its docs also list multi-region deployment (an enterprise feature) and logging of inputs and outputs to buckets the user picks (GCS, S3, Azure Blob), which together let users place stored data where they choose. Missing for 10: an explicit data-residency or region-selection control documented as such, documentation of where cached or spend data is stored by region, and independent or hands-on confirmation of residency handling.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can choose where my data is stored (region/residency)

citations.quote: Self-hosted LLM Gateway (Proxy) with virtual keys, cost tracking, and an admin UI
Multi-region deployment under one license, admin/worker split
Log Proxy input, output, and exceptions using: Langfuse, OpenTelemetry, GCS, s3, Azure (Blob) Buckets
